Ayk and d- prefixed to b-mahzita jointly introduce the comparison as. In a mirror stays separately at 8 and beholding, glory and the Lord are separately linked. The exception covers only the comparative connector.

The feminine target suffix in w-lah anticipates the repeated l-marked feminine likeness noun, a proleptic destination referring to one target. Into the same likeness renders that one resumed destination, not into it and into a second likeness. And remains separately at 10; are transformed and both glory nouns remain separate. This combines only the two case-marked members of the proleptic destination.
Ayk and d- prefixed to men jointly introduce the final comparison as. From remains separately at 17 and the Lord and the Spirit at 18 and 19. Only the comparative connector is shared.

47:4.scope: All original shared spans checked against exact source forms, morphology and context; final changed mappings and running English independently reviewed.

exceptions.reason: Maana lan is the impersonal feminine predicate with an l-marked experiencer, rendered we grow weary. CAL m)n V G2 explicitly describes impersonal feminine plus l as grow weary of, with Syriac examples. Grow weary jointly expresses this construction; we remains separately at 4, do at 3 and not at 2. The dative is not a beneficiary of the service phrase.

Relative d- on the God noun and the third-plural possessive suffix of minds jointly identify whose minds were blinded. Those remains separately at 0, minds at 5 and the God noun at 1, while its own anticipating possessor is specified by this world at 2–3. Only the relative relation and its resumed possessor form whose; no ordinary noun phrase or blinding predicate is shared.

Al with d- prefixed to la forms the causal conjunction because, as described for al d- in Younansardaroud 14.6. Not remains separately at 7 and the believing predicate at 8; the later negative purpose lest is separately at 9. This preserves the causal unbelief clause rather than importing Murdock's purpose wording.

Metul with d- prefixed to the God noun forms because. God remains separately at 1; the following hu focuses God and the saying relative remains at 3. Only the causal connector is shared, without including its subject or predicate.

Ith lan is the possessive existential there is to us, rendered we have. Have jointly expresses the existential and its l-marked possessor; we stays separately at 1, but at 2 and each member of this treasure and the earthen vessel phrase remains separate.

Ith lan is the possessive existential there is to us, rendered we have. Only have combines these two members; we remains separately at 8. The causal d- on one, its focused identity copula and every noun in the spirit-of-faith phrase remain separately linked.

Ayk with d- on the passive written form jointly introduces the comparison as. It is written stays separately at 10, and the following first-person quotation and both because-of-this expressions remain separate. Only the comparative connector is shared.

Man with d- on the raising perfect forms the relative who after that the one. Raised remains separately at 3; our Lord and Jesus, the later us object, future raising, instrumental through Jesus and bringing-near clause are separately linked. Only the relative connector is shared.

Maana lan repeats the impersonal feminine plus l-marked experiencer construction, rendered we grow weary. CAL m)n V G2 explicitly attests this pattern as grow weary of. We remains separately at 4, do at 3 and not at 2; no separate for-us beneficiary is introduced, and the outer/inner-person clauses remain separate.

L-alam almin is the intensive age-of-ages construct idiom for unlimited duration, rendered for ever and ever. The singular construct age with its plural ages jointly expresses that intensified duration rather than two independently counted periods. Only these two idiomatic members are shared; affliction, its modifiers, prepares, for us, great glory and without end all remain separately linked.

47:5.scope: All original shared spans checked against exact source forms, morphology and context; final changed mappings and running English independently reviewed.

exceptions.reason: Ith lan is the possessive existential there is to us, rendered we have. Only have combines the existential and its l-marked possessor; we remains at 10, the building at 11 and from God at 12–13. The house and its modifiers stay individually linked.

Ma with d- on the following clothing perfect forms the temporal conjunction when. We have put it on remains separately at 3 and even at 1. The perfect belongs to a future temporal context; this combines only the temporal connector, not the clothing clause.

The Ethpeal future with lan has a dative co-referential with its first-person plural patient, rendered we shall be found. Only the passive predicate includes that dative; we remains at 5 and naked at 6. It does not introduce another beneficiary or finder, and no negative is inserted into this positive predicate.

L-el men is the compound spatial preposition above or over. Only over combines its two prepositional members; it remains separately at 15, to be clothed at 13, and the mortality, swallowing and life clause remains separate. CAL lists l-yl mn as above, including Syriac usage; men is not silently discarded or made a separate source of the garment.

The feminine suffix in lah anticipates the following l-marked feminine this. Both case-marked members identify the same target of God's preparing, rendered for this rather than for it and for another thing. Prepares, us, God, the copula and the giving clause remain separate.

Metul and d- prefixed to the knowing participle jointly form because. We know stays separately at 1 and therefore at 2; the persuasion, temporal and lodging clauses are separately mapped. Only the causal connector is shared.

Kma with the following d- prefixed to b-pagra forms the temporal conjunction as long as. The preceding complement d- on kma remains separately that at 4, in the body at 5 and we lodge at 6. CAL kmh c explicitly attests Syriac kma d- as long as. This combines only its temporal connector, without absorbing the body or lodging predicate.

Meddem with d- on the following passive done participle forms the anonymous relative what. Has been done remains separately at 12 and by him at 13, preserving the agentive dative without another recipient. The recompense predicate separately owns its English for, and each person, his body and good/evil alternatives remain separate.
Metul and d- on the knowing participle jointly introduce because. We know remains separately at 1 and therefore at 2; fear and its Lord possessor remain separate. Only the causal connector is shared.

Mith leh has a dative co-referential with the immediately preceding singular everyone. English has died renders that single death predicate and its coreferential dative; everyone remains at 12 and therefore at 11. No separate for-him beneficiary or new reference to Messiah is introduced. This is a contextual application of the coreferential motion/experience dative construction.

Ayna with d- prefixed to al forms the relative who after for the one. Died stays at 14 and the al-appay benefactive expression is separately represented by on their behalf at 12–13. Only the relative connector is shared; the death and rising predicates stay distinct.

Al appay with a third-plural suffix is the compound benefactive preposition on their behalf, not a statement about physical faces. CAL al appay explicitly attests Syriac for the sake of/on account of. The d- prefix on al separately contributes to who with ayna at 11; the dying and rising predicates remain separately linked.

Man with d- on the in-Messiah form introduces the relative who. Everyone remains separately at kul0, in Messiah at 2 and its copula at 3. The main is, creation and new are separately mapped; the exception does not include the quantifier or ordinary predicate.

Abar with the feminine plural dative lehein refers to the passing of the old things named at 8. The dative resumes those same old things, not a separate recipient of their passage. English have passed away renders the one motion predicate with its coreferential dative; old things stays separate. This applies the motion-dative construction contextually rather than making an extra for-them clause.

Ayk haw d- forms the hypothetical comparative connector as though, with d- prefixed to the God noun. And remains separately at 5 and God at 7; haw is a demonstrative member of the connector, not an independent is predicate. God's beseeching, its addressee, through us and our subsequent entreaty remain separate, with both therefore particles retained.

exceptions.reason: Ayk and d- prefixed to the chastising participle jointly form the comparative connector as. Being chastised remains separately at 10, and the following conjunction, negative and active dying predicate remain separate. Only the comparative connector is shared.

Ayk and d- prefixed to karya jointly introduce the comparison as. The sorrow predicate and its first-person experiencer are separately represented by sorrowful at 1–2; the connector does not absorb that predicate or the rejoicing contrast.

Karya lan is an impersonal emotional predicate with a first-person plural dative experiencer, rendered sorrowful of the speakers already identified as we. English as sorrowful continues that same first-person plural subject, rather than adding a separate beneficiary to whom someone else's sorrow is directed. Only the emotional predicate with its experiencer is combined; the comparative connector and always rejoicing remain separate.

Ayk with d- prefixed to meddem forms the comparative connector as though. Anything remains separately at meddem10; the following negative existential and its first-person possessor form the separately justified have construction. This does not share the entire having-nothing clause.

The negative existential leith with lan expresses possession, literally there is not to us. Only have combines the existential and its l-marked first-person plural possessor; we remains separately at 12, do and not at 11, and anything at 10. No second owner or beneficiary is introduced.

Ayk with d- prefixed to l-bnaya forms the comparative connector as. To children remains separately at 1; but, I and speak have their own links. No my-children possessor is supplied, and the comparison does not absorb the speaking clause.

Bnay zawga is the lexical son-of-yoke partnership expression, rendered yoke-fellows. Neither sons nor yoke alone expresses the partnership. Only the two members of this lexical expression are combined; be, its negative and those who do not believe remain separately mapped. No absent unequal adjective is introduced.

Ith with l-righteousness is the possessive existential, rendered does righteousness have. Only have combines the existential and its l-marked possessor; does remains at 10, righteousness at 11, and fellowship, with and iniquity remain separate. This does not combine an ordinary noun phrase or the whole question.

Ith with l-light is the possessive existential, rendered does light have. Only have combines the existential and its l-marked possessor; does remains at 17, light at 18, and communion, with and darkness remain separate.

Ith with l-Messiah is the possessive existential, rendered does Messiah have. Only have combines the existential and its l-marked possessor; does remains at 3, Messiah at 4, and concord, with and Satan remain separate.

Ith with l-d-mhaymen is the possessive existential, rendered does one who believes have. Only have combines the existential and its l-marked possessor; does remains at 10 and one who believes at 11. Portion, with and the separately mapped unbelieving relative remain separate.

Ith with l-the-temple is the possessive existential, rendered does the temple have. Only have combines the existential and its l-marked possessor; does remains at 3 and the temple at 4. Of God, with and that of demons remain separate, with no imported idols noun.

Aykana and d- prefixed to the passive said participle jointly introduce the comparison as. It is said remains separately at 15 and the direct quotation begins with the dwelling predicate. Only the comparative connector is shared, not the saying or promise clauses.

D-kul ahid is the all-holding divine epithet, rendered Almighty. The quantifier and holding participle jointly express that title; the Lord remains separately at 9 and says at 8. CAL's ahid adjective entry explicitly lists the Syriac ahid kul expression as almighty. The current relative order is interpreted contextually as the same all-holding epithet, without introducing a second actor or sharing the whole Lord Almighty phrase.

exceptions.reason: Metul with d- prefixed to the existential ith forms because. We stays separately at lan2 and the possessive existential have is separately justified at 1–2; therefore3, these4 and promises5 remain separate. Only the causal connector is combined.

Ith lan is the possessive existential there is to us, rendered we have. Only have combines the existential and its first-person plural l-marked possessor; we remains separately at 2. Because uses the d-prefix of ith with metul0, and the demonstrative and promises remain separate.

Ith li is the possessive existential there is to me. Only have combines the existential and its first-person l-marked possessor; I stays separately at 3, great1 and boldness0 remain separate, and toward you4 is not absorbed.

Ith li is the second first-person possessive existential in the verse. Only have combines the existential and its l-marked possessor; I stays at 7, and5 and much5 are separately exposed, boasting9 and in you8 remain separate. The delayed noun does not require a shared clause.

Men with d- prefixed to the coming perfect forms the temporal conjunction since. We came remains separately at 2, for3 and even0 are separate, and the plural Macedonian gentilic remains at 4. Only the temporal connector is combined, not the coming clause.

Haw with d- on the refreshed predicate introduces the relative referring to his refreshment, rendered with which. He was refreshed remains separately at 7 and by you at 8. The demonstrative and relative identify the same refreshment; they do not turn it into the person who was refreshed or combine the whole clause.

Al appay with a first-person plural suffix is the compound benefactive on our behalf. The d-prefix makes it a modifier of their zeal, not an independent statement about faces. Only the two members of this prepositional idiom are combined; their zeal and its other complements stay separately linked. CAL explicitly attests the Syriac benefactive sense.

Past hwat with li is the possessive existential was to me, rendered I had great joy. Only had combines the existential and its first-person possessor; I remains separately at 24, great at 22 and joy at 21. The ordinary adjective and noun do not join this exception.

Tawya with napshi is the impersonal cognitive expression of regretting or changing one's mind; CAL twy explicitly lists the impersonal construction with napsh. English regret it combines that lexical predicate with its cognitive self component, rather than creating an independently personified soul. Li6 separately identifies I as the experiencer, and do5 and not4 remain separate. The understood object it refers to the preceding grieving by the letter, without another source participant. The later past regret has its own predicate and auxiliary.

Al with d- on the sorrow perfect forms the causal connector because. You remains separately at 8 and the impersonal sorrow construction is separately justified at 7–8. Not5 is separate. The exception includes only the causal connector.

Keryath lekhun is an impersonal emotion construction with a second-person plural dative experiencer, rendered you were grieved. Only were grieved combines the sorrow predicate and its experiencer; you stays separately at 8, because separately uses al6 with d-7, and not5 stays separate. The l-marked addressees are not another beneficiary of someone else's sorrow.
Metul with d- prefixed to your sorrow forms because. Your sorrow remains separately at 11, brought you at 13 and to repentance at 12. Only the causal connector is combined.

Keryath lekhun is the second impersonal sorrow predicate with the addressees as its dative experiencer. Only were grieved combines that predicate and its experiencer; you remains separately at 15, for at 16 and in a godly way at 17. It does not introduce a new person or make the sorrow someone else's action for their benefit.

Aykana with d- prefixed to b-meddem introduces the purpose so that. In anything remains separately at 19, you might and suffer loss at 21, not at 20 and from us at 22. Only the purpose connector is combined, with the imperfect retaining its prospective force.

Mappaq b-ruha is the lexical compound apology or defense, explicitly attested in CAL. Its construct noun and prepositional member jointly express a defense rather than an additional spirit response. And remains separately at 11; diligence, indignation, fear, love, zeal and vindication remain separately linked.

Bah b-tsbutha is a proleptic prepositional construction: the feminine suffix in bah anticipates the following feminine matter with the same b-marker. English in that matter expresses one target rather than in it and in another matter. You showed, yourselves, to be and pure remain separate. This combines only the repeated case-marked target, not the purity clause.

Man with d- on the wronged expression introduces the anonymous relative who. The one remains separately at haw12 and was wronged is separately represented at 14–15. Only the relative connector is combined, not the full wronged-person phrase.

Maskal beh is the analytic wronged-person expression, with beh resuming the same male patient named by the one who. English was wronged includes that patient-resumptive preposition without adding a separate in-him circumstance or another person. The one12 and who13–14 remain separate; neither the purpose nor the offender clause is absorbed.

Metul with d- on the knowing imperfect introduces purpose, rendered so that. Might be known remains separately at 18, your care21 and for us22 remain separate, and before19 and God20 are separately linked. This combines only the purpose connector, not the delayed subject or entire clause.

Meddem with d- prefixed to the boasting perfect forms the anonymous relative what. For and in remain separately at the first d-b-meddem form0, I had boasted at 1 and to him at 2. Only the relative connector is combined; the main not-ashamed predicate remains separate.

Al appay with a second-person plural suffix is the compound benefactive on your behalf in the boasting statement. Its preposition and suffixed faces member jointly express the benefactive relation, not physical faces. The boasting, addressee and negative shame predicate remain separate. CAL explicitly attests the Syriac benefactive sense.

Ayk and d- prefixed to kul jointly introduce as. In all remains separately at 9 and things at 10; we spoke12, truth11 and with you13 are separately mapped. The quantifier is not shared with its ordinary noun, and only the comparative connector is combined.

exceptions.reason: Ayk ma with d- prefixed to the expecting participle forms the comparative connector as. CAL akma d explicitly permits one-word or two-word spellings of ayk ma, with the following relative d-. Only this connector combines its three written members; we and had stay at 4 and expected at 3. Ma does not introduce an additional object of expecting, and the auxiliary is not part of the exception.

Ayk with d- prefixed to the beginning perfect forms as. The complementizer d- on ayk remains separately that at 4, he began at 5 and so at 6. Only the comparative connector is combined, not the beginning or completion clauses.

Aykana with d- prefixed to b-kulmeddem forms as. In everything remains separately at 2 and you4/abound3 are separate. The b-prefix belongs to in, not to the comparative connector; only aykana and the following d- are shared.

Metul with d- prefixed to men forms because. From remains separately at 9, last year at 10 and you began at 11. Only the causal connector is combined; the temporal preposition and year expression remain separate.

Meddem with d- on the desiring perfect forms the relative connector, rendered which after the separately linked demonstrative that4. You desired remains separately at 6. Only the relative connector is combined, without absorbing the desiring clause or the preceding demonstrative.

Aykana with d- prefixed to hwa forms as. The preceding d- on aykana separately owns so that at 7, while the past possessive had is separately justified at 8–9. Readiness10 and to be willing11 remain separate. Only the comparative connector is combined.

Hwa lekhun is the past possessive existential there was to you, rendered you had. Only had combines the existential and its second-person plural possessor; you stays separately at 9 and readiness at 10. The d-prefix of hwa separately participates in as with aykana7.

Ma with d- on the existential ith forms the anonymous relative what. From remains separately at 15, you at 18 and possessive have is separately justified at 17–18. Only the relative connector is combined, not the entire from-what-you-have clause.

Ith lekhun is the possessive existential there is to you. Only have combines the existential and its l-marked possessor; you remains separately at 18. What uses ma16 with d-17, while from15 stays separate.

Ma with d- on ith forms what. According to remains separately at 4, he at 7 and possessive has is separately justified at 6–7. Only the relative connector is combined; the implicit donor is not confused with willingness as an owner of material resources.

Ith leh is the possessive existential there is to him, rendered he has. Only has combines the existential and its l-marked possessor; he remains separately at 7 and what separately uses ma5 with d-6. The acceptance and willingness predicates remain separate.

Ma with d- prefixed to the negative existential leith forms what. He remains at 15, does and not at 14, and the possessive have is separately justified at 14–15. Only the relative connector is combined; the negative is not absorbed into the relative.

Leith leh is the negative possessive existential there is not to him. Only have combines the existential and its l-marked possessor; he stays separately at 15 and does/not separately at 14. The earlier negative focus it is11/not10 and according to12 remain separate, preserving both negations.

Ayk with d- on the written participle forms As. It is written remains separately at 1; the d-prefix on the following demonstrative introduces the direct quotation and is represented by quotation punctuation. Only the comparative connector is shared.

Ethyatar leh describes surplus accruing to the same person who gathered much. English had combines the surplus predicate with its coreferential personal dative, while no stays separately at 5 and surplus separately at 6. The dative does not name another recipient; the gathering predicate and its much modifier remain separate.

Ethbatsar leh describes deficiency with the same person who gathered little as its coreferential dative. English deficient includes that one deficiency predicate and its experiencer; was remains at 12 and not at 11. The dative does not add a separate beneficiary of another person's deficiency, and the gathering/little clause remains separate.
Metul with d- on tab forms because. And remains separately at 3, very at 4, and the concern expression is separately justified at 5–6. Only the causal connector is shared.

Btil leh is an impersonal concern construction with Titus as the dative experiencer; CAL btil number2 explicitly attests concerned with leh. Only concerned combines this predicate and its experiencer; he remains separately at 6, was at 5 and very at 4. It does not add a separate for-him beneficiary, and Titus's own will and going out remain separate.

Ayna with d- on the suffixed praise noun introduces the relative whose. Praise remains separately at 5; its third-person suffix identifies the same brother. Only the relative connector is combined, without sharing the noun or the gospel and ecclesias phrases.

Ayna with d- on lan introduces the relative who. To us remains separately at 6 and has been proved at 7. Only the relative connector is combined; the dative is not silently made an agentive by-us phrase, and always, many things and the diligence predicate remain separate.

47:9.scope: All original shared spans checked against exact source forms, morphology and context; final changed mappings and running English independently reviewed.

exceptions.reason: Aykana with d- prefixed to the saying perfect forms as. So that remains separately at the d-prefix of aykana11, I said at 12, you may be at 13 and prepared at 14. Only the comparative connector is combined, not the saying or preparation clauses.

Men qdim is the compound temporal expression beforehand. Only its two temporal members are combined; the d-prefix on men separately owns which at 14, while that13 and blessing12 are separate. You were informed16, should be17 and ready18 remain separate; the temporal expression does not absorb the hearing or readiness clauses.

Ayk with d- prefixed to men forms as. From remains separately at 7 and sadness at 8; not5 is separate. Only the comparative connector is combined, without sharing the preposition or the ordinary sadness phrase.

Ayk with d- prefixed to men forms the second as. From remains separately at 11, compulsion at 12 and or at 9; the earlier negative governs the alternatives without adding another negative word. Only the comparative connector is shared.

Matya b-iday is the reach-with-hands ability idiom, rendered within the power. CAL mtyG3 explicitly attests the ability construction with b-yd in Syriac Gen31:29 and Acts24:13. Only the reaching predicate and hands member combine; it is remains separately at 1, but at 2 and of God at 4. This does not share an ordinary whole clause or replace the source with another act of God.

Ma with d- prefixed to the sufficing participle forms the anonymous relative, rendered which after the separate demonstrative that11. Is sufficient remains separately at 13 and for you at 14, with may be15 and yours16 separate. Only the relative connector is combined.

Ayk with d- prefixed to the written participle forms As. It is written remains separately at 1; d- on the scattered perfect introduces the direct quotation and is represented by quotation punctuation. Scattering, giving, the poor and the righteousness clause remain separate.

Metul with d- prefixed to the work noun forms because. The work remains separately at 1, of2/this3/service2 are individually linked, and the negative, auxiliary, only and supplying predicate stay separate. Only the causal connector is combined.

exceptions.reason: Ma plus d- on the coming perfect forms the temporal when. I come remains separately at 6, while that and not belong to 4 and the constraint predicate to 7. Only the temporal connector is shared; the perfect is prospective in this subordinate construction.
Ayk plus d- prefixed to the thinking participle forms as. I14 and think13 remain separate, as do toward15 and people16. Only the comparative connector is shared, not the thinking or its complements.

D-ayk with d- on the flesh expression introduces the comparison within their judgment, rendered as though. We walk remains at 22 and according to the flesh at 21. Only the embedded comparative connector combines; its content prefix belongs to the same subordinate judgment and it does not absorb the walking clause.

Ma with d- on the completion perfect forms when. Your obedience remains separately at 9 and has been completed at 8. Only the temporal connector is combined; the completed condition is prospective in context, not a claim it had already occurred.

Ayk14 plus d- prefixed to hu15 forms as. The content prefix on ayk separately owns that14, he is remains at 15, of the Messiah at 16, and so17/also18/are we19 are distinct. Only the comparative connector combines.

Metul with d- on the building noun forms because. For15/your17/building up15 remain separate, with it is and that at the focusing hu16, he gave it18 and to us19 separate. This does not share the delayed giving predicate or the ordinary purpose phrase.

Ayk haw d- forms the irrealis comparison as though. The deictic haw is a dummy head of the comparative clause, not a second terrifier alongside the explicit I9. Only the three connector members combine; greatly7 separately renders the infinitive absolute, terrify8 is the finite predicate, and you10/by my letters11 remain separate. CAL's srp citation Ps-Nonn230(4) attests ayk haw d- with an explicit as-if rendering.

Metul with d- prefixed to the existential forms because. There are remains separately at 1, people2 and who say3 stay separate, and d-4 introduces the quotation through punctuation. The causal clause is connected to verse 9, not left as a subordinate sentence fragment.

Aykana6 with d- prefixed to the existential7 forms as. The content prefix on aykana separately owns that6, we are remains at 7, and the word/letter and absence clauses are split. Only the comparative connector is combined, not the six-word imperative or the existential clause.

Ma plus d- prefixed to the near/present predicate forms when. We are present remains separately at 16 and in deed at 17. The first-person plural suffix belongs to the speakers' presence, not a direction toward them or an unrelated near object.

Metul with d- prefixed to the independent third-plural pronoun forms because. They remains separately at 13, compare at 16, themselves at the lhun15 reflexive and with themselves at bhun14. Only the causal connector is shared; the comparison and its two reflexive arguments remain distinct.

Ayk with d- on the following negative forms as though. The negative itself separately owns not4 and the reaching predicate stays at 5, with you6 separate. The initial negative0 and cleft auxiliary1 remain separate, as do stretch7/ourselves8 and the subsequent past reaching clause. Only the comparative connector combines.

Lhal with men is the compound preposition beyond; CAL lhl explicitly cites this exact verse under the construction with men. Only the directional and prepositional members combine. The second-person plural suffix separately owns you2, also0 and to preach3 stay separate, and the following negative boasting clause is not included.

D- on the named Lord11 and the masculine singular object suffix on the praise verb12 together form the object relative whom. The Lord remains separately at 11 and will praise at 12, preserving the imperfect and one praised object. Only the relative-object connector combines, not the ordinary subject/predicate clause.

47:11.scope: All original shared spans checked against exact source forms, morphology and context; final changed mappings and running English independently reviewed.

exceptions.reason: Ayk with d- prefixed to the deceiving perfect forms as. The serpent6, deceived5, Eve7 and by its craftiness8 remain separately linked. Only the comparative connector combines, not the serpent's action or the recipients' corruption clause.

Ayna with d- prefixed to the independent we pronoun forms the relative whom, referring to the other Jesus. We remains separately at 10, had/proclaimed at 12 and not at 11. Only the relative connector combines, not the negative proclamation clause.

Ayda with d- on the following negative forms which for the other spirit. You had/received remains at 19 and not separately at 18. Only the relative connector is combined, leaving the negative and predicate individually owned.

Ayda with d- on the following negative forms which for the other gospel. You had/accepted remains at 25 and not separately at 24. Only this second relative connector combines; the gospel, alternative and receiving clause are not shared.
Metul with d- on the following negative forms Because. I4, do/love3, not2 and you5 stay separate, as does the subsequent focus statement about God knowing. Only the causal connector combines.

En hu d- is the fixed conditional construction if it is the case that, here rendered if. Hu is a member of that construction, not a new he-is-Satan predicate. Satan remains separately at 6, for at 5, disguises himself at 7 and the angel/light phrase separate. Only the conditional connector combines; CAL en explicitly attests en hu with d-.

Ayk with d- prefixed to the fool adjective forms as though. I were remains separately at 10 and a fool at 9. Only the comparative connector combines, with the English irrealis copula chosen from the hypothetical comparison, not an invented second person.

Ayk with d- on the foolishness expression forms as. In foolishness remains separately at 10, but at 8, in/this at 11, matter12 and of boasting13 separate. Only the comparative connector combines, not the ordinary prepositional or boasting phrase.

Metul with d- prefixed to the many adjective forms Because. Many remains separately at 1, boast2 and according to the flesh3 distinct, with I5/also4/will boast6 separately linked. Only the causal connector combines.

Ayk with d- on the dishonor expression forms as though. In dishonor remains separately at 1, I3 and speak2 distinct. Only the initial comparative connector combines, not the speaker or the following weakness comparison.

Ayk haw d- forms the irrealis comparison as though. Haw is the dummy head of the comparative construction, not another actor alongside we6. We remains separately at 6, were at 8 and weak at 7. Only the three connector members combine; the weakness and the subsequent lack-of-understanding/speaking clauses stay separate.

Repeated forty/forty marks distribution over the five occasions, rendered each time. Only the distributive force of the repeated numeral combines. Forty remains separately at 4; I received and blows belong to the beating verb8, with less6 and one7 separate. The second forty is not falsely treated as an Aramaic noun for stripes, and the entire numeral/subtraction/predicate clause is not shared. Compare Muraoka71a on distributive repetition.

Al appay is the idiomatic preposition on behalf of, rather than literal faces in this concern clause. Only the preposition's two members combine; and my care6, all9 and the ecclesias10 remain separate. The d-prefix on al connects this modifier to the care noun and does not introduce another actor or another care predicate.

47:12.scope: All original shared spans checked against exact source forms, morphology and context; final changed mappings and running English independently reviewed.

exceptions.reason: Independent hu proleptically identifies the following demonstrative hana as the same caught-up man, rendered once as this one.
